newsitem.title: USA: Foreign crudes fetching higher prices in US market.
newsitem.headline: Foreign crudes fetching higher prices in US market.

text.p: A range of foreign crudes were seen fetching higher prices in the U.S. market on Tuesday, reflecting revved-up demand, traders said.
"Everything seems to be getting stronger," a trader said.

The June spread between benchmarks West Texas Intermediate/Midland and North Sea Brent was around $1.55-65 a barrel, about 25 cents narrower than Monday afternoon but still strong enough to fuel transatlantic trade, traders said.
A U.S. company and a European trader were still showing one Brent cargo apiece for end-May and mid-June, respectively.
The companies were asking around WTI minus 70-75 cents a barrel, about five to cents stronger than last week's values, traders said.
Changing economics, however, prompted the U.S. company to bow out of ULCC Laconia for Brent loading around May 5-14 and destined for the U.S. Gulf, trade sources said.
The company is likely to move the cargoes to another market, traders said.
The uptick in foreign crude prices in the Gulf was also relfected in West African levels, traders said.
A European company was showing a 950,000 barrel cargo of Nigerian Bonny Light for arrival on May 27-31 into the Louisiana Offshore Oil Port (LOOP).
The asking price moved up to around WTI minus 20 cents a barrel from a discount of around minus 37 cents last week.

Meanwhile, a U.S. equity producer last Friday sold a Cabinda/Zaire co-loading around May 14-16 to a U.S. refiner. The Cabinda traded at a discount of $1.05 a barrel, while the Zaire fetched minus $1.40.
From Latin America, Chile's state oil company Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (ENAP) was seeking to buy 960,000 barrels of crude oil for delivery around June 25-30, trade sources said.
The tender will be awarded on May 8.

Separately, Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol awarded a cargo each of Cano Limon and South Blend at discounts of $2.97 and $3.30 to benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing on an fob basis, trade sources said.
The Cano Limon cargo, which loads June 13-23, was awarded to a U.S. West Coast refiner.
The South Blend loads June 20-30. The buyer was not disclosed.
